label: Concept
definition: A unit of knowledge created by a unique combination of characteristics.

label: Conceptual Model
definition: An abstract model or representation of data for a particular domain or field of study, independent of any specific software or information system.

label: Data Model
definition: Graphical and/or lexical representation of data, specifying their properties, structure, and interrelationships.

label: Identifier
definition: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.

label: Logical Data Model
definition: A data model that includes all entities and the relationships among them based on the structures identified in a conceptual data model and that specifies all attributes for each entity.

label: Model
definition: A simplified representation or abstraction of a system, process, or concept.

label: Ontology
definition: Specification of concrete or abstract things and the relationships among them in a prescribed domain of knowledge.

label: Physical Data Model
definition: A technical representation detailing how data is physically organized and constrained within a database system, focusing on tables, columns, and constraints rather than entities and attributes.

label: Agent
definition: An agent is something that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.

label: Activity
definition: Something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities; it may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.

label: Collection Object
definition: A physical object that belongs to a museum collection.

label: Compound Specimen
definition: A collection object comprised of one or more discernible parts, called specimen parts, unified by physical attachment. The object's identity is determined by its specimen parts, which are distinguished from one another within a specific context.
usage_note: Central construct of the GCDM. Contrast with Simple Specimen, which carries a single determination and no discernible parts. See GCDM section 3.2.

label: Compound Specimen Model
definition: A conceptual data model in which a single physical object, a compound specimen, is composed of and defined by its specimen parts.

label: Specimen Part
definition: A physically discernible, proximal portion of a compound specimen that carries a single determination and belongs to a single material category, distinguished from the rest of the parent specimen by its physical and chemical exclusivity.
usage_note: The unit of determination in the GCDM. Each Specimen Part carries exactly one determination and belongs to exactly one Material Category. See GCDM section 3.3.

label: Specimen Part Proportion
definition: Refers to the qualitative or quantitative representation of the abundance of a Specimen Part within a parent Compound Specimen.
usage_note: May be recorded qualitatively (e.g. dominant, subordinate, trace) or quantitatively (e.g. percentage). See GCDM section 3.3.2.

label: Specimen Part Relation
definition: A described uni-directional association between two specimen parts, a source and target, within the scope of the parent compound specimen. A relation is defined from the perspective of the source specimen part and described using a relation predicate.
usage_note: Directed from source part to target part and scoped to the parent Compound Specimen. See GCDM section 3.5.

label: Specimen Part Role
definition: Specifies the relationship between a Specimen Part and its parent compound specimen. Roles are dependent upon both the part and parent object. For instance, a rock (material category) within the parent specimen plays the role of clast and is dependent on both the specimen part and the parent specimen for its existence.
usage_note: Roles are contextual: the same material plays different roles depending on the parent object. See GCDM section 3.3.2.

label: Material Category
definition: A value from a top-level, generalized categorization scheme for geologic materials, in which each geologic material, a Compound Specimen or a Specimen Part, belongs to one and only one Material Category. For any given collection, the set of Material Categories should comprehensively account for all parts found across every specimen in that collection.
usage_note: The set of Material Categories used by a collection should be mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive for that collection.

label: Determination
definition: The identity of a specimen represented by a name based on formal criteria evaluated by a domain expert. In biological collections, the determination is represented by a taxonomic classification, primarily a genus and species (e.g., Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii). In the geosciences domain, examples of determination include Almandine, Granite, and Plantae.
examples: Almandine; Granite; Plantae; (biological analogues) Vulpes vulpes, Accipiter cooperii

label: Geologic Material
definition: An amount of matter primarily (dominantly) having parts created by geologic processes and can include minor parts that are not of geologic origin, such as organic material, and can be solid, fluid, or a mix.

label: Geologic Specimen
definition: A collection object comprised, in part, of geologic material.

label: Material Entity
definition: A material entity is an entity that exists in full during the length of time of its existence, persists through this time while maintaining its identity, and has no temporal parts.

label: Object
definition: An object is a maximal causally unified material entity, meaning b is a material entity which is such that its material parts are tied together in such a way that, in environments typical for entities of the type in question.

label: Relation Predicate
definition: Describes the nature of the relationship between two specimen parts within the scope of a compound specimen.

label: Simple Specimen
definition: A collection object identified by a single determination without discernible parts.

label: Simple Specimen Model
definition: The conceptual model for the digital representation of physical specimens where each entity is characterized by one and only one determination without any discernible parts.

label: Alternate Name
definition: An alternate lexical label to the preferred term for an entity.

label: Authoritative Name
definition: A name sanctioned by an authority based on a defined set of unambiguous criteria and belonging to a formal nomenclature.

label: Authority
definition: Identifies the entity responsible for assigning and maintaining a formalized classification system.

label: Classification
definition: Activity involving grouping similar or related things together; separating dissimilar or unrelated things; and arranging the resulting groups in a logical and helpful sequence.

label: Classification Code
definition: Encoded classification of an object represented by a graphical symbol that conforms to an encoding scheme defined as part of the classification scheme.

label: Classification Family
definition: A grouping of related classification series (skos:Collection); e.g., all mineral classifications.
usage_note: Modeled as skos:Collection. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

label: Classification Item
definition: A single node of a classification scheme, one concept or named entry, modeled as a skos:Concept, to which a Specimen Part is classified.
usage_note: Modeled as skos:Concept. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

label: Classification Item Relation
definition: A reified, directed parent–child edge between two Classification Items that constitutes the hierarchy, typed by skos:broader/skos:narrower.
usage_note: Reified edge typed by skos:broader / skos:narrower. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

label: Classification Level
definition: A stratified tier comprised of nodes with a shared level of granularity in a hierarchy.

label: Classification Name
definition: A formalized name belonging to a classification system maintained by an authoritative body.

label: Classification Rank
definition: An identifier assigned to a classification level commonly expressed using a numeric identifier or lexical label.

label: Classification Rank Relation
definition: A reified ordering relation between two Classification Ranks, present only for ranked schemes.
usage_note: Present only for ranked schemes. See GCDM section 4.5.3.

label: Classification Scheme
definition: A method of organization according to a set of pre-established principles, usually characterized by a notation system and a hierarchical structure of relationships among the entities. This standard defines the structure and organization of a classification system, including its hierarchical ranks.

label: Classification Series
definition: The time-ordered set of successive versions of one classification (skos:OrderedCollection); e.g., the editions of Dana.
usage_note: Modeled as skos:OrderedCollection. See GCDM section 4.5.3.
examples: The successive editions of the Dana classification

label: Classification System
definition: A terminological resource that has characteristics of mutual exclusiveness and exhaustiveness to aggregate data to a pre-prescribed level of specialization for a specific purpose. Extends the classification scheme concept to include the values used to populate a classification scheme.

label: Classification Term
definition: A single concept in a classification system or scheme at any hierarchical level.

label: Classification Version
definition: A versioned instance of a classification scheme.

label: Confirmation Protocol
definition: The procedure by which a Name is verified or confirmed for a specimen.
usage_note: Carried by the determinedBy relation in GCDM Figure 10.

label: Depth
definition: The numeric distance of a nested level from the root of a hierarchy in a stratified classification scheme.

label: Hierarchy
definition: Concept system in which all concepts are related in hierarchical relations that form a partial ordering.

label: Identification
definition: The process of recognizing an entity in a particular domain as distinct from other entities.

label: Linnaean Taxonomy
definition: A classification system for grouping both living and extinct organisms, governed by the relevant nomenclatural codes (the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature for animals; the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants). Generally, the parent-child relationships in the Linnaean hierarchy represent the lineage evolution between species.
usage_note: Governed by the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature for animals and the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants.

label: Monohierarchy
definition: Hierarchical arrangement of concepts in a classification scheme in which each concept can have only one broader concept at the level immediately above.

label: Name
definition: The primary means of identification of objects and concepts for humans.

label: Name Type
definition: The category of a Name, Specimen, Authoritative, or Alternate, assigned through the hasType relation.
usage_note: Assigned through the hasType relation in GCDM Figure 10.

label: Naming Authority
definition: A registration authority that allocates names according to specified rules.

label: Nomenclature Status
definition: The standing of a Name within its nomenclatural system (e.g., approved, superseded), recorded through the hasStatus relation.
usage_note: Recorded through the hasStatus relation in GCDM Figure 10.

label: Specimen Name
definition: Refers to any name assigned to a specimen at the object level (before atomization into specimen parts). Specimen names are often written as compound terms, a concatenation of multiple informal and formal identifiers.
usage_note: Applies at the object level, before atomization into specimen parts; often a concatenation of informal and formal identifiers.

label: Value Set
definition: The range of values used to populate a classification scheme (or classification scheme variant).

label: Biostratigraphic Unit
definition: Geologic units defined or characterized on the basis of their contained fossils. Biostratigraphic units exist only where the particular diagnostic feature or attribute on which they are based has been identified.

label: Chronostratigraphic Unit
definition: Bodies of rocks, layered or unlayered, that are defined between specified stratigraphic horizons which represent specified intervals of geologic time.

label: Geologic Unit
definition: A body of rock that persists through time, forming a discrete and definable unit. Geologic units are identified by their geometric, compositional, and internal structural characteristics, as well as their spatio-temporal relations with other rock bodies.

label: Geologic Unit Type
definition: A scheme that specifies concepts used to categorize types of geologic units. Unit types are differentiated based on their defining composition, temporal context, or other physical properties.
examples: Lithostratigraphic; Chronostratigraphic; Biostratigraphic; Magnetostratigraphic; Tectonostratigraphic; Lithodemic

label: Law of Superposition
definition: A general law upon which all geologic chronology is based, where younger lithostratigraphic units lie atop older lithostratigraphic units.

label: Lithodemic Unit
definition: A defined body of predominantly intrusive, highly deformed, and (or) highly metamorphosed rock, distinguished and delimited based on rock characteristics.

label: Lithology
definition: (a) The description of rocks, especially in hand specimens and outcrops, based on characteristics such as color, mineralogic composition, and grain size. (b) The physical character of a rock.

label: Lithostratigraphic Unit
definition: A defined body of sedimentary, extrusive igneous, metasedimentary, or metavolcanic strata that is distinguished and delimited based on lithic characteristics and stratigraphic position.

label: Magnetostratigraphic Unit
definition: Bodies of rock strata unified by similar magnetic characteristics which allow them to be differentiated from adjacent strata.

label: Stratigraphy
definition: The description of all rock bodies forming the Earth's crust and their organization into distinctive, useful, mappable units based on their inherent properties or attributes in order to establish their distribution and relationship in space and their succession in time, and to interpret geologic history.

label: Tectonostratigraphic Unit
definition: Geologic unit defined on basis of structural or deformation features, mutual relations, origin or historical evolution. Contained material may be igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic.

label: Geochronologic Boundary
definition: Temporal boundaries defined with reference to some geologic evidence such as, for instance, fossil appearance/disappearance or significant change in local rock lithology.

label: Geochronologic Era
definition: A named interval of geologic time of any rank, used to express a Relative Age as a bounded ordinal interval.
usage_note: Used to express a Relative Age as a bounded ordinal interval. See GCDM Figure 22a.

label: Geochronologic Interpretation
definition: An interpretation made by a geologist of the age of a specimen made by statistical analysis of a single collection of observations. A specimen may have multiple geochronological interpretations made on it, each related to a different observation collection.

label: Geochronologic Rank
definition: The hierarchical level of a Geochronologic Era, Eon, Era, Period, Epoch, Age, carried through the hasRank relation.
usage_note: Carried through the hasRank relation in GCDM Figure 22a.

label: Geochronologic Unit
definition: A specialized time ordinal interval used to subdivide geologic time based on a corresponding chronostratigraphic unit.

label: Geochronology
definition: The science of determining absolute ages of geologic events and Earth materials. The primary technique utilizes radioactive isotopes and the production and accumulation of radiogenic daughter isotopes naturally present on Earth. It can be applied to various samples, including rocks, minerals, and biological materials.

label: Geologic Event
definition: An identifiable event during which one or more geologic processes act to modify geologic entities.

label: Geologic Process
definition: A natural process that affects the geologic record by acting upon one geologic entity to produce another geologic entity at a later time.

label: Geologic Timescale
definition: A temporal reference system that subdivides all the time since Earth formed into named intervals (units) of abstract time and subdivides all the rocks formed since Earth formed into the successions of rock formed during each particular interval of time.

label: Chronometric Age
definition: The age of a geologic event that resulted in the formation of a geologic material, expressed numerically and based on the results of a dating technique such as radiometric dating or dendrochronology. The value is an interpretation of the timing of that event rather than a direct, certain measurement of the specimen's age; it is conventionally termed absolute age, and also radiometric or apparent age.
usage_note: Conventionally termed absolute age, and also radiometric or apparent age. See GCDM section 6.4.

label: Lower Temporal Boundary
definition: The older (earlier) limit of an interval, the point in time at which the interval begins. By convention, older is "lower" (deeper in the stratigraphic column).
usage_note: By convention, older is 'lower' (deeper in the stratigraphic column).

label: Radioactive Decay
definition: The process where an unstable parent isotope loses particles from its atomic nucleus (decay) to form a daughter isotope (product) at a constant rate.

label: Radiometric Age
definition: Geologic age expressed in years determined by quantitatively measuring radioactive elements and their decay products.

label: Radiometric Dating
definition: Determination of a numeric (absolute) age by measuring the relative abundances of a radioactive parent isotope and its stable daughter product, together with the known decay constant, in a mineral or rock.

label: Regional Timescale
definition: A family of geologic timescales based on the strata and fossil record observed in a specific area, typically at the country or regional level.

label: Relative Age
definition: The geologic age of a fossil organism, rock, or geologic feature or event defined relative to other organisms, rocks, or features or events rather than in terms of years.

label: Relative Dating
definition: Proper chronological placement of a feature, object, or happening in the geologic time scale without reference to its absolute age.

label: Time Interval
definition: A temporal entity with an extent or duration.

label: Upper Temporal Boundary
definition: The younger (later) limit of an interval, the point in time at which the interval ends. By convention, younger is "upper."
usage_note: By convention, younger is 'upper'.

label: Feature
definition: Abstraction of real-world phenomena.

label: Feature of Interest
definition: A feature of interest is an abstraction of a real-world phenomenon that is being sampled or transformed in an act of Sampling.

label: Geologic Environment
definition: Physical conditions found on the Earth's surface, which are determined by factors such as climate, tectonics, physiography, geography and within the Earth's interior, determined by pressure, temperature, chemical environment, and tectonics.

label: Geologic Event Environment
definition: The physical setting within which a Geologic Event takes place.

label: Geologic Feature
definition: A physical or conceptual feature that is hypothesized to exist coherently in the Earth and that results from geologic processes.

label: Material Sample
definition: A physical result of a sampling (or subsampling) event. Material samples are typically collected and either preserved or destructively processed.

label: Petrographic Province
definition: A broad area in which similar igneous rocks are formed during the same period of igneous activity.

label: Physiographic Feature
definition: A natural feature of the solid surface of the Earth or other planetary body.
usage_note: The manuscript cites 'FAO 2025' alongside INRAE 2021 for this definition; that citation is not resolved in the manuscript bibliography.

label: Physiographic Province
definition: A region in which all parts are similar in geologic structure and climate and which has consequently had a unified geomorphic history; a region whose pattern of relief features or landforms differs significantly from adjacent regions.

label: Province
definition: Any large area or region considered as a whole, all parts characterized by similar features or a history differing significantly from adjacent areas.

label: Quarry
definition: An open or surface mineral working, usually for extracting building stone, such as slate, limestone, etc. It is distinguished from a mine because a quarry usually is open at the top and front, and, in ordinary use of the term, by the character of the material extracted.

label: Sample
definition: A feature which is intended to be representative of a `FeatureOfInterest` on which `Observations` may be made.

label: Sampling Event
definition: An activity of Sampling carries out a (Sampling) Procedure to create or transform one or more Samples.

label: Sampling Feature
definition: The feature of interest a sample is intended to be representative of.

label: Sampling Feature Type
definition: The nature of the feature such as whether the feature is the result of natural processes.

label: Sampling Location
definition: The geographic place where a sampling event takes place.

label: Tectonic Province
definition: Groups of provinces linked by a common tectonic history are designated tectonic provinces. Tectonic provinces may contain a collection of sedimentary, igneous, structural, metamorphic, and metallogenic provinces.

label: Tectonic Setting
definition: A geologic event environment defined by relationships to tectonic plates on or in the Earth.

label: Terrane
definition: A fault-bounded area or region with different layers, rock structures, and geologic history from nearby areas that are not connected to them by unconformable contacts or changes in the rock's surface.

label: Mine
definition: A work for excavating minerals using pits, shafts, levels, tunnels, etc., as opposed to a quarry, where the whole excavation is open. In general, the existence of a mine is determined by the mode in which the mineral is obtained, not by its chemical or geologic character. The term also includes only excavations for their minerals or valuable mineral deposits.
